start_here: Say to your AI: "Fill bakery/TEMPLATE.json with 52 loaves, sourced from my Monday log in bakery/log.txt line 1." It runs tool:fill-a-word-template and writes bakery/filled.md.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON. For this folder the account row holds your own dimensions registry.
alike: a config sheet or settings spreadsheet
a notes page of defaults per project

instructions: 1. Make the template first with tool:make-a-word-template (its TEMPLATE.md lists each slot id, here auto-number-w2).

2. Write a fills file, for example bakery/fills.json: {"title":"Monday bakery line","root":".","fills":{"auto-number-w2":{"value":"52","sources":["bakery/log.txt:1"]}}}. Each value needs a checkable source (a URL, git:<repo>@<commit>, or a file line like bakery/log.txt:1) whose text holds the value's words and numbers.

3. Say to your AI: "Fill bakery/TEMPLATE.json from bakery/fills.json". It reads the row with tools:list and runs python3 -I tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/fill.py bakery/TEMPLATE.json bakery/fills.json bakery/filled.md --piece bakery/filled.md.piece.json

4. Read bakery/filled.md: the script, the line view with the sourced value in « », the sources table with each check, and the empty slots with what would fill them. A value with no checkable source stays empty as [TYPE: no source yet]; never invent a source.
5. A fill can change slots only; an id that is not a slot is refused. Judge the result with tool:check-words-against-a-word-template.
6. Optional: if you keep your own dimensions registry as a row of list:settings, read that row with records:read, write it to a file and add --settings-record FILE to the command.

worked_examples.title: Fill the loaf count from a log line
worked_examples.ask: Fill my template with 52 loaves from my Monday log.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/fill.py and run for real with the template of tool:make-a-word-template and a fills file giving auto-number-w2 the value 52 with source bakery/log.txt:1 (that line reads "Monday log: 52 loaves came out of the oven."): python3 -I tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/fill.py bakery/TEMPLATE.json bakery/fills.json bakery/filled.md --piece bakery/filled.md.piece.json
worked_examples.hands_back: Exit 0 and the line: bakery/filled.md: 1 slots filled from checked sources, 0 empty, 0 offered without a valid source (left empty). bakery/filled.md holds the script "Sam baked 52 loaves before dawn and sold them all." and a sources row: auto-number-w2, NUMBER, 52, bakery/log.txt:1, found in bakery/log.txt:1.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for tool settings and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and list:settings as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
